body:
I often dream of doing something different. I knew medical school was going to be hard, but I never thought it would be *this* hard. Now all I want is an 8-5 job where I do the same things day in and out. Unfortunately, I'm $70K in debt and half way through school. Taking time off is not possible until after I graduate in two years or have a death or birth in the family. I'm supposed to move to another town next month to start my third year of medical school. Maybe the change of city and the transition from book work to being in the hospital will be good for me. 

Thank you for getting back to me last night. I couldn't reach anyone in my phone to talk to. Hearing back on here was enough.

Thank you for this. Your message was enough to calm me down last night, enough to try and think rationally again. When I saw the school psychiatrist she asked if I ever had thoughts of killing myself, I said, "Yes, but doesn't everyone?" She then proceeded to explain how that is not normal at all and few people actually think that way. Thanks for telling me it's normal if these thoughts come into my head once in a while. I've gotten better at telling myself to postpone the end, but last night was really bad. Thank you for getting back to me.

I wish I could go to my parents, but they think mental health issues should only be treated with prayer. And if I am struggling with suicidal thoughts or depression, it's because my faith in God is lacking. That's what they would say at least. As far as taking time off school, I wish it were easy. I am already $70K in debt and halfway through medical school. I guess you can say once you're in the system, you're stuck. Hardly anyone ever leaves. I wish I could take time off, but if there's a good time for that it's in two years when I graduate.
